title: Infosys Names Three-Decade Veteran Ashiss Kumar Dash as Next CEO
excerpt: The IT giant tapped insider Ashiss Kumar Dash to succeed Salil Parekh from April 2027 while trimming its full-year revenue growth forecast, sending US-listed shares down 5%.
body:
• Infosys appointed company veteran Ashiss Kumar Dash as CEO designate, succeeding Salil Parekh from April 1, 2027, after a 31-year career spanning delivery, sales and energy verticals.
  • The company narrowed its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1.5%–3.0% from 1.5%–3.5%, citing soft volumes, a client program termination and macroeconomic uncertainty.
  • Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14% year-on-year to ₹48,211 crore but missed analyst estimates, while AI services climbed to 8.2% of total revenue from 5.5% just two quarters earlier.

Infosys has named company veteran Ashiss Kumar Dash as its next chief executive, choosing a three-decade insider to lead India's second-largest IT services firm through what the industry calls an AI-driven upheaval in technology spending. The succession plan, announced alongside the company's first-quarter results on Thursday, was paired with a cut to full-year revenue guidance that sent US-listed shares down roughly 5% in early trading.

Dash, currently executive vice president and global head of the energy, utilities, resources and enterprise sustainability verticals, will take over as CEO and managing director on April 1, 2027, for a five-year term. He succeeds Salil Parekh, the longest-serving non-founder CEO in Infosys history, whose second five-year term ends in March.

"Ashiss Kumar Dash is a safe, execution-focused appointment at a time when Infosys needs stability as much as transformation."

— Phil Fersht, CEO, HFS Research

A Calculated Internal Pick

Chairman Nandan Nilekani said the board prioritised a leader who could "drive bold transformation" while preserving the client trust that has distinguished Infosys. Dash, an IIT Kharagpur alumnus who also completed Stanford University's Global Leadership Program, has held senior roles across client-facing businesses, delivery and global operations spanning multiple geographies, according to the company.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=3sMoEXxlNIA

Dash will relocate from Los Angeles to India in the coming months and begin a structured handover, with Parekh expected to mentor him from October. Under Parekh's nearly decade-long tenure, Infosys roughly doubled its revenue from $10 billion to more than $20 billion and laid the groundwork for its AI strategy.

"Salil has done a stellar job as the CEO for almost 10 years," Nilekani said, crediting Parekh with transitioning Infosys into the digital era.

Revenue Miss and Narrower Guidance

The leadership announcement arrived alongside a mixed set of quarterly numbers. Revenue for Q1 FY27 rose 14% year-on-year to ₹48,211 crore ($5.08 billion), but missed the LSEG analyst consensus of ₹48,367 crore. Net profit climbed 12.2% to ₹7,769 crore, also falling short of the ₹7,832 crore estimate.

CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka attributed the shortfall partly to a one-off 50-basis-point revenue hit from a programme termination by a client in the energy vertical and volumes that were "soft and weaker than expectations." Infosys narrowed its constant-currency revenue growth guidance for FY27 to 1.5%–3.0%, trimming the upper end from the earlier 3.5%. Analysts had expected a range of 2.5%–4.5%, according to Reuters.

Operating margin held up at 21.1%, rising 20 basis points sequentially, and the company maintained its full-year margin guidance of 20%–22%. Free cash flow came in at $955 million, or 116.5% of net profit, while the balance sheet remained debt-free with $3.9 billion in cash.

AI Revenue Surges as Clients Shift Spending

A bright spot was the rapid growth of AI-linked services, which accounted for 8.2% of total revenue, up from 5.5% in the December quarter. Parekh said more than 80,000 Infosys employees are now working with coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex on client and internal projects. The company plans to build a team of 6,000 "frontier engineers" over the next few years.

Large deal bookings totalled $3.6 billion across 22 contracts, with 61% classified as net new business. Three individual deals were worth approximately $400 million each. Sanghrajka said 20% of large deal value came from vendor consolidation opportunities, positioning Infosys "on the positive side" of that trend.

Wage Hikes, Hiring and the Road Ahead

Infosys plans salary increases for most employees effective October, with senior staff covered in January 2027, Parekh said. The company still intends to recruit 20,000 college graduates during the fiscal year, having already onboarded more than 4,000 in Q1. Total headcount dipped slightly to 328,062, and the trailing 12-month attrition rate edged up to 13% from 12.6%.

Rivals Tata Consultancy Services and HCLTech both beat quarterly estimates earlier, aided by strong financial services demand and a weaker rupee, making Infosys's revenue miss and guidance cut stand out.

"Technology is entering a new era, with AI fundamentally reshaping how businesses operate and create value."

— Ashiss Kumar Dash, CEO Designate, Infosys

Dash's appointment signals Infosys is betting on institutional continuity rather than an external shake-up as it navigates the AI transition. Investors and clients will be watching whether the insider can balance cost discipline with the aggressive AI investments the $315 billion Indian IT sector increasingly demands.
image_caption: Ashiss Kumar Dash, a three-decade Infosys veteran, has been named the company's next CEO effective January 2027
nri_angle: Infosys is a major employer of Indian professionals worldwide and its CEO transition and AI strategy shift could reshape career opportunities across its global delivery centres.
